headline: Firmus, the Nvidia-backed Australian data-centre builder, pulled its share sale after asking investors to value it at $30 billion on just $51 million of revenue for the year.
score_reason: Viral floor 7: 26 outlets carry the Firmus IPO story (VIRAL RULE, Rafi, 10 Oct 2026); curator score was 5
importance_line: What changed is that the price and revenue behind a failed AI share sale are now known, which matters first to savers and pension funds that would have been asked to buy, then to data-centre builders that depend on outside money, and the doubt is that one company's failed sale may not signal a wider cooling.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as carried by the Taipei Times, that Firmus, an Australian data-centre builder backed by Nvidia, dropped its share sale on 9 Oct 2026 after investors balked at the US$30 billion valuation it sought, up from US$10.5 billion less than three months earlier, on revenue of US$51 million in the 2026 financial year. New since our 9 Oct 2026 edition, which reported the cancelled sale (Reuters), are the revenue behind the price and investor documents, seen by Bloomberg, showing only 46 of its planned 912 megawatts of data-centre capacity is built.
notes: URL is the Taipei Times page where the Bloomberg text was read; the pool's Benzinga original was blocked (HTTP 403). Authorship of the Bloomberg attribution inferred from the text's references to Bloomberg.
